description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of various BERT-based models across three evaluation metrics—Sentiment Accuracy (light yellow), STS Correlation (light pink), and Paraphrase Accuracy (light blue)—on five different model configurations: Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, Supervised_SimCSE, and an unlabeled gray bar at the far right (likely a placeholder or omitted category). The vertical axis represents “Accuracy / Correlation” on a linear scale from 0 to 0.8, with major tick marks at 0.2 intervals. Across all models, Paraphrase Accuracy consistently achieves the highest values, ranging from approximately 0.77 to 0.79. STS Correlation shows the most variation, starting at ~0.50 for Single-task_baseline and rising to ~0.81 for both Supervised_SimCSE and the final unlabeled category. Sentiment Accuracy remains relatively stable across models, hovering between ~0.48 and ~0.53. The Supervised_SimCSE model achieves the highest STS Correlation (~0.81), while the Single-task_baseline performs best on Sentiment Accuracy (~0.53). The chart visually emphasizes that SimCSE variants (both supervised and unsupervised) significantly boost STS Correlation compared to baseline models, while maintaining strong performance on Paraphrase Accuracy. The legend at the top clearly maps each color to its corresponding metric, and the x-axis labels are evenly spaced, indicating a comparative evaluation rather than a temporal or ordered progression.
